Package org.jdesktop.lg3d.displayserver.desktop2d

Class VolumeStatus

java.lang.Object
org.jdesktop.lg3d.displayserver.desktop2d.VolumeStatus
public final class VolumeStatus extends Object
Master output volume for the 2D taskbar indicator, the Control Center Sound panel and the system-indicators widget.

The clamping, dB↔percentage maths, CLI output parsing, command building and formatting are pure (clamp(int), percentFromDb(float, float, float), dbFromPercent(int, float, float), parseWpctl(java.lang.String), parsePactlVolume(java.lang.String), parsePactlMute(java.lang.String), parseAmixer(java.lang.String), the *Command builders, glyph(org.jdesktop.lg3d.displayserver.desktop2d.VolumeStatus.Level), label(org.jdesktop.lg3d.displayserver.desktop2d.VolumeStatus.Level)) and unit-tested; the read/write methods are thin probes over the host's audio tooling.

Backends are tried most-authoritative first, because on a PipeWire or PulseAudio desktop the javax.sound.sampled master port is either absent or - worse - reports a stale ALSA view that does not track the real sink volume:

  1. PipeWire via wpctl (Fedora 31+, modern distros);
  2. PulseAudio via pactl;
  3. plain ALSA via amixer - the Linux From Scratch / minimal case, where there is no sound server and alsa-utils drives the card directly;
  4. javax.sound.sampled master port, as a last resort for hosts with none of the above tools (e.g. macOS, Windows, or a bare JDK).

Every probe returns Optional.empty() / no-ops when no master control exists (headless CI, no sound card, no tool installed), so the indicator hides itself and the panel shows its "no audio device" note instead of failing.
